Privacy Policy

Last updated October 14, 2026

This Privacy Policy explains how Homesolo LLC, a District of Columbia limited liability company operating Homesolo (“we,” “us,” or “Homesolo”), collects, uses, and protects your information, and the rights you have under the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). Homesolo is not available in California.

Information we collect

  • Name and email address
  • Property information you enter (addresses, attributes, notes)
  • License numbers (for brokers)
  • AI-generated outputs (pricing analyses, descriptions, offer evaluations)
  • Payment information (processed by Stripe; we do not store full card numbers)
  • MLS data, used temporarily for display only (see below)
  • Your Bright MLS member ID, which we check to verify your license, and the license number and state you give us
  • Information about other people that you enter: your clients, prospects and other contacts (name, email, phone, role, notes, activity, follow-up dates), their saved search criteria and labels, and offer details that name a buyer. You are responsible for having a right to enter it; we keep it only to provide the service to you and do not use it for any other purpose
  • Technical and security records: IP address and sign-in attempts, and a record that an AI question was asked and what it cost (not its text)
  • In your browser: your session cookies, your cookie preference, your theme, and, in the tab, the conversation you have had with Joy, which can contain client names. It is removed when you sign out or close the tab

Third parties we share data with

We use the following sub-processors, each only for the purpose stated:

  • Anthropic — AI processing (inference only). No MLS data is sent to Anthropic.
  • Bright MLS — source of property listing data. Bright requires usage monitoring on pages that show its data; when that is enabled, a script supplied by Bright runs on those pages
  • Google — converts a property address to map coordinates (geocoding)
  • Stripe — payment processing
  • Resend — transactional email delivery
  • Supabase — application data hosting and authentication
  • Sentry — error monitoring (with PII scrubbing)
  • Upstash — rate limiting and caching
  • Vercel — application hosting and delivery (processes requests and request logs, including IP addresses)

Public property records

Assessor records, building permits and recorded sales for the District of Columbia, Maryland and Northern Virginia come from those governments’ own public files: the DC Office of Tax and Revenue and the DC Department of Buildings (published by DC GIS); Maryland’s Department of Assessments and Taxation, including its assessment (CAMA) building file and its file of recorded sales (published by Maryland iMAP); the building-permit files of Montgomery County and Prince George’s County; and the real-estate assessment and sales files of Fairfax County (Department of Tax Administration), Arlington County (Department of Real Estate Assessments) and Loudoun County. We download the files whole and match properties on our own servers. No information about you, your clients, or the properties you look up is sent to these agencies.

We do not download the names of property owners, buyers, sellers or permit applicants from these files. Maryland publishes its sales file twelve months at a time; we keep each recorded transfer we download (date, price and type of transfer), so the history we can show grows over time.

MLS data

Property listing data from Bright MLS is used solely to display real estate information within our platform. MLS data is not transmitted to any AI provider. Bright MLS data is not used to train or improve any AI model.

AI processing

We use Anthropic’s API for inference only. Your content — the information you provide and the AI-generated outputs you receive — is not used to train any AI model, by Anthropic or anyone else. MLS listing data is never sent to any AI provider; the AI receives only abstracted summaries.

Joy, the in-app assistant, works from Homesolo’s own figures and placeholders. Client names, email addresses, phone numbers and property addresses that you have saved in Homesolo are replaced with placeholders before anything is sent, and we put the real details back into her answer after it returns. Text you type yourself is sent as you wrote it, so a name that is not saved in Homesolo, or a spelling that differs from the saved one, may not be replaced: say “my seller” instead of a name. The same is true of other AI features that take free text or a document you upload (listing descriptions, counter-offers, questions about an analysis, contract reading), which send what you give them. We keep a record that a question was asked and what it cost, not its text.

Your rights

Subject to applicable law, you have the right to access your data, to rectify inaccurate data, to request erasure of your data, and to portability (a machine-readable export). You can export or delete your data at any time from Settings → Privacy.

Data retention

  • Active data is retained while your account is active.
  • When you delete your account, your profile and the records you own — properties, listings, analyses, documents, and the transactions attached to your properties — are deleted immediately.
  • Where you were a counterparty to another user’s transaction, that transaction record remains with the other party, with your link to it removed.
  • Security logs (sign-in attempts) are kept for 7 days, and payment-webhook records for 90 days, after which they are purged automatically.

Contact

For privacy requests, contact privacy@homesolo.ai.

      - /url: /apply
  - main:
    - paragraph: Decision intelligence for real estate professionals
    - heading "The CMA that shows its work, with the data most CMAs leave out." [level=1]
    - paragraph: Then it tells you what to do about it.
    - paragraph: Homesolo runs every comparable sale, active listing, permit, assessor record, expired listing, price cut, seller concession, market supply level, current competition, true days on market, this week’s mortgage rate and more through one pricing engine, then turns it into a strategy you can defend, and helps you advise, negotiate and close.
    - link "Apply for the Founding Beta":
      - /url: /apply
      - text: Apply for the Founding Beta
      - img
    - link "See an example CMA":
      - /url: /demo
    - paragraph: Built for licensed brokers, agents and salespeople in DC, Maryland and Virginia. Every license verified. The founding beta is free.
    - text: 214 Maple Row Illustrative sample
    - paragraph: Recommended list price
    - paragraph: $1,075,000
    - paragraph: Conservative
    - paragraph: $1,040,000
    - paragraph: Moderate
    - paragraph: $1,075,000
    - paragraph: Aggressive
    - paragraph: $1,120,000
    - paragraph: Homesolo intelligence
    - paragraph: Listed inside the supported comparable range and below the top of it, leaving room to negotiate.
    - heading "More information isn’t the advantage. Knowing what to do with it is." [level=2]
    - paragraph: Your MLS gives you market data. Your CRM organizes your contacts. AI can help you research and write. And your own experience gives you judgment. But the hardest part of real estate has never been accessing information — it’s knowing what to do with it.
    - paragraph: Homesolo turns the information surrounding your business into decisions you can act on — and reasoning you can defend to your clients.
    - heading "The decisions that make or break a listing." [level=3]
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: Price with evidence.
        - paragraph: Comparable sales, current competition and market speed become three positions, each with its tradeoff, so the seller sees the reasoning and not only your opinion.
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: Launch with a plan.
        - paragraph: "One decisive position, then a tracked test: showings, second showings, offers and what buyers said."
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: Stop the drip.
        - paragraph: When response is weak, Homesolo shows whether it is the price, the presentation or the market, so you can make one decisive move instead of five small cuts.
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: Never fly blind.
        - paragraph: Each week Homesolo re-reads the market against your listing.
    - paragraph: What’s happening. Why it matters. What to do next.
    - paragraph: Built for the DMV
    - heading "Built for the DMV." [level=2]
    - paragraph: Homesolo is built specifically for the DMV — DC, Maryland and Virginia — with the region’s own inventory, pace and pricing patterns built in from the start.
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: Runs on Bright MLS.
        - paragraph: Every comparable, adjustment and recommendation comes straight from Bright MLS data.
      - listitem:
        - paragraph: More than the MLS alone.

More information isn’t the advantage. Knowing what to do with it is.

Your MLS gives you market data. Your CRM organizes your contacts. AI can help you research and write. And your own experience gives you judgment. But the hardest part of real estate has never been accessing information — it’s knowing what to do with it.

Homesolo turns the information surrounding your business into decisions you can act on — and reasoning you can defend to your clients.

The decisions that make or break a listing.

  • Price with evidence.

    Comparable sales, current competition and market speed become three positions, each with its tradeoff, so the seller sees the reasoning and not only your opinion.

  • Launch with a plan.

    One decisive position, then a tracked test: showings, second showings, offers and what buyers said.

  • Stop the drip.

    When response is weak, Homesolo shows whether it is the price, the presentation or the market, so you can make one decisive move instead of five small cuts.

  • Never fly blind.

    Each week Homesolo re-reads the market against your listing.

Frequently asked questions

Who is Homesolo for?

Licensed real estate brokers, agents and salespeople working in DC, Maryland, and Virginia. We verify every license by hand before the workbench unlocks.

What is a CMA, and how does Homesolo build one?

A comparative market analysis estimates what a home is worth from comparable recent sales. Homesolo selects the comparable sales, adjusts them for differences such as size and condition, and shows the value range together with the evidence behind it. The pricing math is deterministic, so the same inputs give the same numbers.

Where does the market data come from?

Homesolo works from the Bright MLS feed under a data license. Listing data is shown with its required broker attribution and a freshness stamp.

How much does Homesolo cost?

The founding beta is free, with full platform access and free training from the founders. We will share pricing well before the beta ends.

When does the free beta start?

When your license has been verified and your workbench is unlocked, not when you sign up, so the time you have is time you can actually use the product.

How does broker approval work?

After you sign up we check your license and MLS membership by hand. Until that is done the workbench stays locked. It exists to make sure the tools go only to licensed brokers.

Can Homesolo tell me when to change a listing’s price?

It reviews your live listings against the market every week and tracks buyer response at check-ins: showings, second showings, offers, and what buyers said. It then lays out what to consider and why. It is guidance for you as the broker, not automatic and not a forecast, and nothing changes a price or contacts anyone on its own.

What is Joy, and what can she see?

Joy is Homesolo’s assistant for licensed brokers. She knows the CMA, offer or transaction you are looking at, explains Homesolo’s analysis, reads an offer, and drafts messages to your clients. She works from Homesolo’s own figures and placeholders: client names, emails, phone numbers and property addresses you have saved in Homesolo are swapped for placeholders before anything is sent, and filled back in on your screen. Text you type is sent as written, so say “my seller” rather than a name. She gives decision support, not legal advice. You review and send everything yourself.

How does Homesolo handle fair housing?

Every generated description is checked against a fair-housing prohibited-terms list before it is delivered. Violations are blocked and logged.

How accurate is the AI?

AI output is informational and is not a professional appraisal or legal advice. Pricing math is deterministic; AI narration explains it. You are responsible for reviewing all output.

How is my data handled, and is any AI trained on it?

Your data is scoped to your account with row-level security. MLS listing data is never sent to the AI; only abstracted summaries are. No model is trained on MLS data, and our AI provider’s commercial terms do not train on what we send it.

Child-process extraction covers asynchronous node:child_process creation, literal argv/env/stdio options, exit/error listeners, and kill signals.
Configuration extraction covers process.env, process.argv, node:fs reads, and direct logical defaults.
Event extraction covers EventEmitter-style literal registrations, removals, and dispatch candidates; dynamic names remain unknown.
Function fingerprints are static candidates; equal digests can remain ambiguous and do not prove behavioral equivalence.
Local data flow does not claim control-flow-sensitive reaching definitions or arbitrary dynamic property resolution.
Promise ownership covers explicit unshadowed Promise construction, static factories, aggregation, chaining, and await syntax only.
Request extraction covers fetch, WebSocket, node:http/node:https construction, direct option fields, and exact local response consumers.
Resource extraction covers built-in filesystem/network acquisition and exact local close/destroy/end handles.
The semantic graph contains static syntax observations and conservative relationship candidates; it does not claim runtime execution.
Timer extraction covers global or node:timers scheduling and exact local-handle cancellation.
